standard.summary: 标准 LoRA 的输出缩放为 alpha/rank；开启 RS-LoRA 时为 alpha/√rank。它会影响训练，但不能直接等同于学习率。
standard.effect: 标准 LoRA 中，alpha=rank 时输出缩放为 1；alpha=rank/2 时为 0.5；alpha=1、rank=16 时为 1/16。这些是相同 A/B 权重下的输出比例，不是学习率比例。
standard.whenToUse: 可从已有配方的 alpha=rank 或 rank/2 起步。改变 rank、alpha 或 RS-LoRA 时，应一起检查初始化方式和学习率，不假设原配方的更新幅度不变。
standard.avoidWhen: 提高 alpha 会放大相同 A/B 权重的输出；标准 LoRA 在 alpha>rank 时缩放大于 1，RS-LoRA 则在 alpha>√rank 时大于 1。不要仅凭这个边界判断训练是否稳定；若实际 scaling 为 0，LoRA 分支没有输出或任务梯度。

standard_en.summary: Standard LoRA scales its output by alpha/rank; RS-LoRA uses alpha/sqrt(rank). This affects training but is not equivalent to the learning rate.
standard_en.effect: For standard LoRA, alpha=rank gives output scale 1; alpha=rank/2 gives 0.5; alpha=1 with rank=16 gives 1/16. These ratios compare identical A/B weights, not learning rates.
standard_en.whenToUse: An existing recipe using alpha=rank or rank/2 is a starting point. When changing rank, alpha or RS-LoRA, review initialization and learning rate together rather than assuming unchanged update magnitudes.
standard_en.avoidWhen: Raising alpha amplifies the output of identical A/B weights. Scaling exceeds 1 when alpha>rank for standard LoRA, or alpha>sqrt(rank) for RS-LoRA. This threshold alone does not establish training stability; if actual scaling is zero, the LoRA branch has no output or task gradient.

advanced.principle: 标准 LoRA 的 ΔW = (alpha/rank) × B × A，RS-LoRA 改用 alpha/√rank。A、B 都会更新，实际 ΔW 的变化还取决于初始化、rank 和优化器，不能只用 lr×scaling 推导。
advanced.tradeoffs: μA 研究表明，rank 的学习率迁移规律依赖初始化及有效缩放。论文中的 alpha 指 BA 的有效乘数，不等于这里的 network_alpha；保持 alpha/rank 不变也不能保证收敛速度不变。

advanced_en.principle: Standard LoRA uses ΔW = (alpha/rank) × B × A; RS-LoRA uses alpha/sqrt(rank). Both A and B are updated, so changes in ΔW also depend on initialization, rank and optimizer rather than lr×scaling alone.
advanced_en.tradeoffs: μA shows that learning-rate transfer across ranks depends on initialization and effective scaling. Its alpha denotes the multiplier on BA, not this network_alpha. Keeping alpha/rank fixed does not guarantee unchanged convergence speed.
